title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic Dieudonné theory
summary: A completed target-level planning and independent review pass for prismatic Dieudonné theory, with 83 nodes in eight planned layers and 15 explicit closure gaps. The target is the contravariant classification of p-divisible groups over quasi-syntomic rings. Corrected frame, duality, display and étale-site conventions; imported the parent-owned coefficient comparison; and moved the upward Hodge–Tate input here. The review requests changes because the unrestricted Zink–Lau proof and its identification with the specific prismatic display functor remain unverified. Nothing here is claimed to be formalized.
readme:
The full roadmap, API outlines, tests and review obligations are in research/blueprint/readmes/PrismaticCohomologyPartII.md.

This Part II plans prismatic Dieudonné theory over quasi-syntomic rings, with the contravariant convention BT(R)^op ≃ DM^adm(R). The parent PrismaticCohomology owns prisms, cohomology, Nygaard filtrations, twists and the coefficient vector-bundle comparison. AInfCohomology owns BKF linear algebra; this roadmap owns the admissible prismatic interpretation. The Hodge–Tate map/sequence and general display convention are owned here so that this tier-13 bundle imports no higher roadmap.

The target-level pass is complete, with explicit gaps in site/internal-Ext infrastructure, compatible covers, period-theoretic inputs, crystalline coefficients and display comparisons. The independent review requests changes: the unrestricted Lau08 proof and its comparison with the specific display functor remain unverified. This is a plan, not formalized mathematics.

Scholze–Weinstein uses the naive dual of the contravariant module, with p⁻¹-normalized covariant crystalline Frobenius. Česnavičius–Scholze uses composition with Cartier duality. These conventions are distinct. Other routed directions (crystalline local systems, F-smoothness and integral Riemann–Hilbert) remain separate proposed roadmaps.

stages.title: Frames, windows and minuscule Breuil–Kisin modules
stages.description: General Cais–Lau frames with Fil A+pA in the radical, windows and normal decompositions over henselian pairs; oriented bounded-prism frames; finite-projective minuscule modules, their projective cokernels and the Cais–Lau equivalence; unit-Frobenius and window deformation with explicit complete topologies. Sources: CL17 §2.1, pp. 4–7; AL23 §4.1, pp. 32–39.

stages.title: Quasi-syntomic coefficients and prismatic Dieudonné crystals
stages.description: Relative big and small quasi-syntomic sites, sheafified inverse image, coefficient sheaves and their Nygaard quotient; henselianity; admissible prismatic crystals/modules, their stack and filtered forms, and Nygaard windows. Import the vector-bundle equivalence from the parent PR.7 instead of duplicating it. Ringed-site infrastructure is an explicit gap. Source: AL23 §§3.3 and 4.1, pp. 22–23, 27–39.

stages.title: The prismatic Dieudonné functor
stages.description: Functorial resolution and derived Yoneda; the contravariant internal-Ext Dieudonné functor and its pushforward and Tate-module descriptions. Construct the needed internal Ext sheaves rather than identify them with Mathlib global Ext. Compatible infinite quasi-syntomic root covers are a recorded gap. Source: AL23 §§4.2 and 4.4, pp. 39–43, 52–53.

stages.title: The perfectoid case
stages.description: Own the p-divisible Hodge–Tate map/sequence; Scholze–Weinstein pairs and BKF classification over 𝒪_C; formal abelian covers and crystalline realization; the integral-perfectoid classification and its prismatic identification. Distinguish the absolute PD envelope and p⁻¹ covariant normalization. The Hodge–Tate proof, period-image/rigid inputs, Witt v-descent and nonnoetherian effectivity remain gaps. Sources: SW13 §5; SW20 Lectures 12, 14, 15 and Appendix 17; AL23 §4.3.

stages.title: Abelian schemes, finiteness, admissibility and crystalline comparison
stages.description: Exterior Hodge–Tate/prismatic cohomology of abelian schemes, primitive elements, Ext finiteness, admissibility and Lie quotient; finite and truncated BT Ext crystals; crystalline and classical comparisons and exactness. At p=2 retain the precise abelian-lifting gap. Mixed-characteristic crystalline coefficient evaluations require their own compatible construction. Source: AL23 §§4.3, 4.5–4.6, pp. 43–65.

stages.title: The classification of p-divisible groups
stages.description: q-logarithm, étale/multiplicative calculations and Cartier duality; weight-one kernel formula with the source G/G* correction; full faithfulness, essential surjectivity and the main contravariant classification. The explicit inverse uses Frobenius-compatible linear maps to O^pris, avoiding an undefined integral Frobenius on the naive dual. Sources: AL23 §2.2 and §§4.6–4.9, pp. 14–16, 63–74; BL22 Theorem 7.5.6.

stages.title: Finite locally free group schemes over perfectoid and perfect bases
stages.description: Torsion Dieudonné triples over perfectoid rings, exact base change and finite locally free group classification. Cartier duality uses Ext¹_A(M,A)⊗M_Δ(μ_{p∞}), with operators induced from a dual isogeny presentation. Include the Česnavičius–Scholze covariant normalization and perfect-base crystalline classification. Sources: AL23 §5.1, pp. 75–77; Lau18 §10, pp. 26–29; CS24 §§4.1–4.2, pp. 36, 41.

stages.title: Regular local rings, displays and the étale comparison
stages.description: Import regular perfectoid towers, prove automatic admissibility and the one-variable Breuil–Kisin comparison with its separate characteristic-p connection gap; identify Kisin via the parent Fargues-pair compatibility. Own Witt frames, all-window displays, the correctly normalized Nygaard map, general formal groups and the display functor. The unrestricted Zink–Lau comparison is unverified; its printed prismatic proof is retracted. Étale comparison distinguishes the integral v-site, α and generic-fibre j. Sources: AL23 §§5.2–5.4, pp. 78–93 and erratum; Zink02; Lau08 attribution only.
